recipes.name: Zuppa Toscana
ingredients_raw: 2 cups kale - washed, dried, and shredded

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Arrange sausage links onto a baking sheet; bake in the preheated oven for 25 minutes, or until cooked through. Cut in half lengthwise, then cut at an angle into 1/2-inch slices.
Place onions and bacon in a large saucepan; cook and stir over medium heat until bacon is crispy and onions are tender. Remove bacon and crumble; set aside.
Add garlic; cook for 1 minute. Add bouillon powder, water, and potatoes; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add crumbled bacon, sausage, kale, and cream. Simmer for 4 minutes and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Zuppa Toscana
raw_recipe.description: Zuppa Toscana is a creamy, hearty Italian soup that's packed with flavor thanks to the addition of smoked sausage, garlic, and kale.

review.reviewBody: Great flavor. I'm a health nut so I doubled up on the kale and only used half the sausage as some have suggested. I also replaced the full-fat sausage with turkey kielbasa, which still gives great flavor. I used canned white Northern beans instead of potatoes since I was in a hurry. If you want the creaminess in the soup without all the fat, blend a drained can of Northern white beans with chicken broth (to the consistency you want)instead of the cream. I used chicken broth instead of the water(the brand Imagine has a boxed broth that costs the same as a can for the amount -- it's the best broth I've tasted). Also, you can get the same great flavor with only three or four pieces of bacon.

I worked at olive garden as a front line cook and helped make the zuppa. Need to use italian sausage (OG uses crumbled...I prefer sliced) and not smoked sausage. We also used chicken broth with chicken powder. Can use 1/2 and 1/2 instead of heavy cream as if you add too much, it over powers the broth.

I have made this soup several times and it is always a very welcomed meal, but I do change it a bit. I add diced carrots and I do not use the chicken bouillon, but instead use no salt chicken broth and smoked turkey sausage. I add all ingredients to my slow cooker (with the exception of the heavy cream and kale...I add those and allow them to blend in about 30 minutes before serving). This warming soup goes great with a side salad and garlic toast...a perfect meal for a cooler temperature night.

This soup is so delicious but I do make a few changes. I cut up the sausage in rounds (and half again per the receipe) but instead of baking it I fry them in the big pot that I am making the soup in (remove when cooked and put back later), then scrape the pot out to continue with the rest of the recipe. I also cut the russet potatoes in cubes instead of slices (easier to eat). I use more garlic probably 1 tablespoon and cook with the onion. Instead of bouillon powder & water, I use 2 litres of chicken or veg broth (unsalted). And to save calories I used 250 ml of half and half cream. I add the kale with the potatoes as it takes quite some time to cook. I cut the kale into strips and then cut them a few times as I find the long strands are hard to eat. The bacon I cook in strips and then cut up (as your garnish). An excellent soup that we have regularly. I haven't tried it yet but I bet you could easily substitute spinach for kale but what a great way to use your kale.

Inspired by this recipe. I changed the smoked sausage to Italian Mild, I replaced the Chicken Bouillon and water with Low Sodium Chicken Broth (about 42oz). I browned the Italian sausage in a dutch oven, removed them, drained the dutch oven, added some saved bacon grease, fried the onions for 3 minutes, and garlic for 60 seconds. I then added the broth and sausages. Brought it to a boil then added the potatoes. Let simmer for 45 minutes until the potatoes were done. Added the crumpled bacon, kale,and about 1/2 cup cream. Yum!

I've been using this recipe for over a year now. I do use both spinach and kale only because I love the taste of both of them. I put in either Andouille sausage or Cajun sausage with hot Italian sausage, and red pepper flakes (Calabrian chilis) they add a nice flavor and a little zing to it. This recipe by itself is very good, I just prefer a little more kick and I love spinach mixed with kale. It isn't to make it healthier either because I believe that it healthy enough just the way it is! I make this and freeze it and just use it as necessary. I couldn't do it last time because everyone ate it all!

I made a batch of this soup in October for the cool California nights to come. I think it was fantabulous! I had to make a few substitutions to accommodate what I had on hand…mild Italian sausage, 32oz containers of chicken broth and stock, and added a few spices. I live alone so the batch will last me for several meals, unless I share which is my intention! Hope you all enjoy!

I have to say I took this recipe and ran with what I had and it was delicious. I used homemade sweet Italian sausage, browned in a skillet with sweet onion. I used a quart and a half of chicken broth, fresh mushrooms and golden potatoes. I brought it to a boil then reduced heat to low and let it simmer. About half an hour before dinner, I added chopped fresh baby spinach and canned milk. Served with garlic cheddar bassy biscuits. Whole family loved it.

My family enjoyed this meal. Even my kid who doesn't like soup said he could eat it, just isn't his favorite. However, that is better than refusing to eat it!!! I didn't use heavy cream to save on calories. We added a dollop of sour cream to make it seem creamier. Also used mild Italian sausage with gave it so much flavor. We will be making this again. I also cooked the sausage, onions, bacon ahead of time and added the rest of the ingredients to the slow cooker. Then added the bacon,sausage mix to the slow cooker and cooked on high for 3 hrs. I love my slow cooker for busy days!!

4 Stars as written. I only use 1/2 pound of sausage. Use hot Italian Chicken sausage, and remove the meat from the casing, browning it in large "crumbles". I use low-sodium chicken broth instead of the bouillon and water to cut down on sodium. If I have thick sliced bacon on hand, I only add 3 slices. It is best with heavy cream, but, I don't usually have it on and and use 1/2 & 1/2 (which I always have). It still tastes fantastic. Hubby says it's better than Olive Garden.

Good soup and worth trying first following the recipe. When I made it a second time, I did make some changes. Instead of the packaged smoked sausage, I used a mild Italian Turkey sausage and removed it from the casing & browned. I also fried the bacon in the oven, let it cool and then crumbled it into the soup when the potatoes were almost finished cooking. I also believe I used spinach when I could not find kale that looked good. The last two editions were to make the soup creamier. So I increased the heavy cream to 1 c and also used a can of evaporated milk. Enjoy!

I tweaked it a little and used spicy chicken bullion instead of water. 1 box of spicy, and one box of regular chicken bullion. I also used two thirds of a pound of Italian sausage. Used four cups of spinach instead of kale too. Love it!
My family loved this and asked if we could have it again. Thank you!

There are only 2 of us, so I-made roughly half the recipe and used what I had on hand. I use 4.1 oz Italian sausage which I removed casings and cooked in oven, 2 small red potatoes, 1/2 cup chopped onion, 3 slices bacon , 3/4 tsp minced garlic, a hefty cup of kale, 2 cups reduced chicken broth, and approximately 3 tbsp of cream. Delicious! I am sure original recipe is too but this recipe is very versatile and easy to change with what you have.

We really enjoyed this, great flavour. I used premade frozen bacon stock instead of bouillon cubes, and frozen blitzed kale. I couldn't get smoked sausage, but it worked with Italian style sausages off the shelf. Next time I'll cold smoke these first.

My son made this for us several times, it's a family favorite. I'm not really a fan of kale, but they all love it. He's doubled the (sweet Italian) sausage, and a few times made it keto friendly using turnips instead of potatoes. Honestly it's a great recipe.
